learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of fundamental Thermodynamics.
Apply state equations to different thermodynamic systems.
Understand the concept of thermodynamic work and apply it to specific cases.
Understand the first principle of Thermodynamics.
Understand the different thermodynamic processes and the notion of enthalpy.
Understand the equilibrium equations of a rigid body and know how to apply them in specific situations.
Calculate centers of gravity of bodies with different geometries.
Distinguish the different types of rigid body motion in specific cases.
Calculate moments of inertia and apply the notions of energy and angular momentum to a rigid body.
Understand the concept of linear mechanical wave.

syllabus_topics: Unit Systems: Definition of unit system
Unit Systems: The International System of Units (SI). Basic and derived units
Unit Systems: Conversion factors between units. The case of temperature
Fundamental Thermodynamic Concepts: Thermodynamics. Thermodynamic systems. Classification
Fundamental Thermodynamic Concepts: Macroscopic and microscopic description of a thermodynamic system. Thermodynamic variables
Fundamental Thermodynamic Concepts: State of a system. State of thermodynamic equilibrium
Fundamental Thermodynamic Concepts: Thermodynamic transformations or processes. Quasi-static and non-static processes. Thermodynamic interactions. T-V and p-V diagrams
Fundamental Thermodynamic Concepts: Energy concepts: work, heat, internal energy and enthalpy
Thermal Equations of State. Ideal and Real Gases: Equation of state of a system
Thermal Equations of State. Ideal and Real Gases: Laws of ideal gases. Thermal equation of state of the ideal gas
Thermal Equations of State. Ideal and Real Gases: Real gas. Thermal equation of state of the real gas. Compressibility factor
Pure Substances. Thermodynamic Diagrams and Tables: Pure substance. Homogeneous mixture
Pure Substances. Thermodynamic Diagrams and Tables: Phase diagram. Saturation curve
Pure Substances. Thermodynamic Diagrams and Tables: Saturation tables. Compressed liquid and superheated vapor tables
Pure Substances. Thermodynamic Diagrams and Tables: Quality or title of a mixture. Humidity degree
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Calculation of the work involved in the change of volume of a system
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Heat capacities. Calculation of heat transferred in a process
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Formulation of the First Principle for a closed system
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Joule's Law. Isothermal process of an ideal gas
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Energy equation of state of a system
First Principle of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems: Energy balance in an ideal gas. Calculation of the enthalpy of an ideal gas
Fundamental Thermodynamic Processes: Polytropic processes. Polytropic index
Fundamental Thermodynamic Processes: Equations of fundamental processes of ideal gas. Work calculation
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Rigid body (RB)
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Internal and external forces
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Principle of transmissibility. Equivalent forces
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Systems of sliding vectors. Varignon's Theorem
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Equilibrium equations of the RB
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body: Free body diagram
Centers of Gravity and Distributed Forces: Systems of parallel forces. Center of parallel forces. Center of gravity (CG)
Centers of Gravity and Distributed Forces: Determination of the CG. Centroids. First order moments
Centers of Gravity and Distributed Forces: Properties of the CG of a system
Centers of Gravity and Distributed Forces: Pappus-Guldinus Theorems
Centers of Gravity and Distributed Forces: Distributed loads on beams
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Moment of inertia of an area or second order moment
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Polar moment of inertia
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Radius of gyration of an area
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Steiner's Theorem
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Calculation of moments of inertia of composite areas
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Moment of inertia of a body
Moments of Inertia of Areas and Bodies: Laboratory practice: moment of inertia of a disk. Verification of Steiner's Theorem
Kinematics of a Rigid Body: Different types of rigid body movements
Kinematics of a Rigid Body: Translational motion: velocity and acceleration
Kinematics of a Rigid Body: Rotational motion: velocity and acceleration
Kinematics of a Rigid Body: Rototranslational motion: velocity and acceleration. Rolling motion. Helical motion
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Center of mass of a body (CM). Velocity and acceleration of the CM
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Equation of Translational Dynamics of a rigid body
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Linear momentum of a body. Conservation theorem
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Angular momentum of a body
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Equations of Rotational Dynamics of a rigid body
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Conservation theorem of angular momentum
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Kinetic energy and work in the rigid body motion
Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Potential energy of a rigid body. Energy conservation
Mechanical Waves: Laboratory practice: mechanical waves. Standing waves. Transverse waves in strings
assessment_rules: The final grade in continuous evaluation is calculated as 80% from the Final Written Exam (EFE), 10% from Laboratory Practices, and 10% from Questionnaires. To pass, the EFE score must be at least 4 out of 10, with its Thermodynamics (TERMO) and Mechanics (MEC) parts each scoring at least 3 out of 10, and the overall final grade must be 5 or higher. A partial eliminatory exam for Thermodynamics is offered, allowing that part to be waived if passed with 5/10 or more. If conditions are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4. The global evaluation modality follows a similar grading structure, but no partial exam scores are retained for subsequent calls.
